title: Outbound newsletters: subscriptions, scheduled issues and sending through SES
description:
Papyrus publications send their own newsletters: readers subscribe on the public site, editors compose issues in the newsroom, admins approve each issue for a scheduled time, and the site backend sends it through Amazon SES with no person or laptop involved at send time. First client: Distinctive Mark (distinctive-mark.com, newsletter "The Docket", weekly plus precedential alerts by topic); its public site already has the signup forms and subscribe page, posting to newsletter.signupEndpoint (null until this ships).

Distinct from epic 68d06c (Email and newsletter monitoring intake), which READS other publications' newsletters. This initiative SENDS ours.

Decisions (Ryan, 2026-10-20):
- Storage follows the card-catalog rule: DynamoDB indexes (issue records, schedules, send ledger, event aggregates) in the existing Papyrus data schema; S3 holds the shelves (rendered issue HTML and text, web archive copies, raw SES events).
- Subscriber records are personal data, not content: encrypted, kept apart from the content schema, never readable through the guest or editor content API, admin-only export.
- Only admins approve a send. Nobody presses a live Send: approval schedules the issue for a time (EventBridge Scheduler, stored in UTC, shown in the publication time zone). At fire time the send run re-checks that the issue is still scheduled and unchanged since approval (content hash); an edited issue returns to draft and nothing is sent.
- A recurring cadence (The Docket, every Friday) assembles a draft and notifies admins; it never sends without an admin approval for that issue. No approval, no issue.
- Paid newsletters are out of scope (YAGNI).

Constraints to design for:
- SES sending quota, reputation and sandbox are per account and region, and every site lives in papyrus-production: one site's bounces or complaints can pause sending for all sites. Per-site configuration sets, sending subdomains and alarms that pause one site before AWS pauses the account.
- Gmail/Yahoo bulk-sender rules: SPF, DKIM, aligned DMARC, one-click unsubscribe (RFC 8058 List-Unsubscribe-Post) honoured within two days, spam rate under 0.3%.
- CAN-SPAM postal address and unsubscribe in every message; consent proof per subscriber (time, form, wording shown, confirmation) for GDPR/CASL; double opt-in; erasure on request.
- Sponsored blocks may be attorney advertising (Distinctive Mark's sponsor is a lawyer) and must carry the same labelling as on the site.
- A per-site feature flag (PAPYRUS_ENABLE_NEWSLETTERS); the email template and sponsor slots are a per-site plugin seam like the SiteProjector.

comments.text: Distinctive Mark (AnthusAI/Distinctive-web, Kanbus project dist) is the first client: its signup forms, subscribe page and newsletter settings (web/site-config.json newsletter block) wait on M1; its issues f4e5f5 (connect signups) and 51f1c1 (The Docket weekly email) map to M1 and M2.

comments.author: home
comments.text: Ryan 2026-10-21: build sending now, all of the standard stuff: double opt-in, approved weekly roundup, on-demand alerts when items are published. Shipped (shipped.anth.us) is enabled first, Distinctive Mark second. Design: a newsletter plugin (amplify/plugins/newsletter) with a KMS-encrypted plugin table for subscribers (not an Amplify model), a per-site CloudFormation sending stack (infra/newsletter), CMS Next routes under /api/newsletter/* (already routed at every edge), a Python renderer (src/papyrus_content/email_render), roundup issues as Items of a configured type (published on send, so the archive gets a page, Markus twin and llms.txt), and alerts hooked on the publish event (not procedure runs), deduplicated per item lineage per list. Postal address is a required plugin setting that blocks issue and alert sends while unset. Stories: 874ad4, 4158a2, 949d68, b5a699, 64f38a (M1); 7643d1, 3ae3b9, 4005de (M2); d415c0, 237074, 93b135 (M3).

comments.text: Status 2026-10-22: released in Papyrus 5.21.0 (promotion #545): sending stack, renderer, double opt-in, unsubscribe and suppression, roundup approval and paced sending, publish-triggered alerts, newsroom panel. Live on Shipped (Shipped-web #30, #33) and verified with the SES mailbox simulator. Docs live at p.apyr.us/newsletters.html. Text fixes in #550 (develop). Waiting on the human inbox test (confirm, test alert, one-click unsubscribe), then Distinctive Mark (needs postal address choice and DNS timing).
